prompt: Construct a SilverOak Operations Suite supporting offline-first procurement, inventory governance, and activity accountability for a multi-site care institution. Users include Institution Admins who configure departments and approvals, Medical Staff who request and consume supplies, Seniors and Family Members who view approved supply usage and wellness activity summaries, and Approvers (department heads or finance) who review requests. In the Yew web UI, staff create a material requisition by selecting items from an on-hand catalog, entering quantities, needed-by date (MM/DD/YYYY), and a justification; the screen shows current stock, unit price, and a projected total against a configurable cap (for example, auto-route to Finance when a requisition exceeds $2,500.00 or contains controlled categories). Approvers get an inbox with side-by-side request details and prior comments, can approve, reject with a required reason, or send back for edits; requestors can withdraw while pending. Every decision appends a timestamped comment to an audit view that is readable but not editable. For consumable ordering, the UI provides a cart and checkout experience that supports merging same-store and cross-store carts, warns when bundles or thresholds are close (for example, “Add $15.00 more to qualify for bulk pricing”), enforces promotion stacking rules (one coupon per order, member pricing cannot stack with threshold discounts, purchase limit of 5 units per SKU per day), calculates a local delivery method fee schedule (pickup $0.00, internal courier $7.50, scheduled delivery $12.00), and performs a final “verify” step that re-checks price and inventory before confirming. The backend uses Actix-web to expose REST-style APIs consumed by the decoupled Yew frontend over the local network, with PostgreSQL providing durable persistence for master data, mappings, orders, requisitions, approvals, and audit logs. Master data management supports CRUD and bulk import/export (Excel/CSV) for students/classes/departments/courses/semesters as organizational reference tables, enforcing uniqueness and referential integrity; imports run format validation, column whitelisting, and file fingerprint checks to prevent tampering, and invalid rows are rejected with line-level feedback. A configurable approval engine stores approval nodes, role bindings, and conditional rules (by spend limit and category); once final approval is recorded, the system automatically generates an outbound issue record and deducts inventory in a single database transaction to prevent partial updates. Multi-role access control is RBAC-based for menus, APIs, and data scopes (institution/department/staff/family group), with permission-change auditing and session-based login using locally verified usernames and hashed passwords (minimum 12 characters, lockout after 5 failed attempts for 15 minutes); account recovery is admin-mediated via offline identity checks rather than email/SMS. System configuration includes environment separation (dev/prod), encrypted-at-rest secrets in PostgreSQL, and mini-program style API security with signed requests, short-lived tokens (15 minutes), timestamp anti-replay (±60 seconds), per-IP rate limits (e.g., 120 requests/minute), and IP blacklisting. Security and compliance capabilities include TLS for in-transit encryption within the local environment, field-level encryption for sensitive notes, data minimization with explicit consent flags for family-visible content, anomaly detection for frequent-request patterns and privilege-escalation attempts, and content safety review via local keyword policies and manual moderator queues. Unified ID and feature mapping tables maintain consistent user/product identifiers with incremental updates, conflict detection, and nightly consistency validation jobs, while an analytics module aggregates daily/weekly/monthly activity stats, trends, PBs, and goal completion using scheduled local jobs with no external dependencies.
